title: Amid Middle East tensions: Foreign Ministry sets up Emergency Response Unit
summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has established an Emergency Response Unit to ensure the safety of Sri Lankans living in the Middle East, due to the tense situation prevailing in the region. Issuing a special notice, the Foreign Ministry announced the following telephone numbers and email address for contact in any emergency: Emergency Response Unit, Ministry of Foreign Affairs: +94117445641 / +94112207250, WhatsApp only: +940777189552, Email: emergency.sl@mfa.gov.lk, Consular Affairs Division, Ministry of Foreign Affairs: +94742595546, Sri Lanka Bureau of Foreign Employment: +94719802822, and Hotline: 1989. This service is open to Sri Lankans employed in the Middle East region or to their relatives residing in Sri Lanka to obtain any necessary assistance.

title: Following enactment of Inland Revenue Bill: TIN to become mandatory for many services
summary: By Sulochana Ramiah Mohan Following the enactment of the Inland Revenue (Amendment) Bill, which has already been gazetted, a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) certificate will become mandatory for a range of services. Accordingly, individuals will be required to present a TIN certificate when opening an account at any financial institution, obtaining approval for a building plan, registering a motor vehicle or renewing a vehicle licence, registering land or land ownership, registering a business, transferring shares of a company incorporated in Sri Lanka by a transferee, and obtaining credit cards. The new requirement is expected to come into effect from April.

title: GL urges Govt to address Middle East fallout
summary: By Sulochana Ramiah Mohan Former Foreign Minister Prof. G.L. Peiris has written to President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, warning that the ongoing crisis in the Middle East could have serious and immediate repercussions for Sri Lanka. Writing on behalf of concerned citizens, Prof. Peiris stressed the need for the Government to promptly communicate its position to both the public and the international community. The letter further noted that the crisis affects Sri Lanka in at least four key areas. First, escalating global oil prices are expected to drive up local fuel costs, significantly increasing the cost of living and aggravating the economic hardships already faced by the public. Second, export revenues, particularly from commodities such as tea, may decline due to restricted access to key markets affected by active military conflicts in the region. Third, the tourism and hotel sector is already experiencing considerable cancellations from prospective tourists from Europe, North America, and the Gulf, who face difficulties related to air travel across the affected regions. Fourth, the situation threatens the viability of remittances from Sri Lankan workers throughout the Gulf and wider areas, which are a critical source of foreign income for the country. Prof. Peiris stressed that citizens are prepared to assist the Government in addressing these multifaceted challenges and are actively discussing practical measures to mitigate the crisis’s effects. A public briefing is planned in the near future to share these discussions and proposals. He also urged the Government to release basic information on its approach to the crisis. This, he said, would allow the public to participate in an informed manner and help ensure transparency in navigating these troubling developments.

title: SJB condemns recent attack on Iran – Sajith
summary: By Sandasen Marasinghe Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa, yesterday (3), revealing the stance of the Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB), condemned the recent attack on Iran and called on the Sri Lankan Government to issue a similar statement. He added that Parliament should not be divided on this matter and should maintain a unified stance on the attack against a sovereign nation. He also condemned the retaliatory attacks targeting the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, and Bahrain. Addressing Parliament following President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, Opposition Leader Premadasa said the Government should not be reluctant to condemn the attack, as it constitutes a clear violation of international law, including Articles 2(4) and 2(7) of the United Nations Charter. He added that another nation could respond under the provisions of Article 51, which allows for self-defence. “We should not be divided as a Parliament on this matter and should maintain the same stance,” the Opposition Leader said. He further proposed that the entire House should condemn the attack as an assault on a sovereign nation. He added that it would be positive if the Government issued a statement condemning it, as the Government need not fear doing so. He also urged the Government to condemn retaliatory attacks targeting the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, and Bahrain. Premadasa also suggested that the Government should revise its agreement with the IMF, particularly the debt sustainability analysis included in the policy statement of the NPP. He highlighted the issue of settling USD 3 billion in 2028, noting that he raised this matter while the President addressed fuel concerns in Parliament. He said the SJB was ready to support the Government in this endeavour. title: Minister Karunathilaka says: 205 flights cancelled due to Middle East tensions
summary: By Sulochana Ramiah Mohan Minister of Ports and Civil Aviation Anura Karunathilaka stated that the civil aviation industry has not yet returned to normalcy following the escalation of tensions in the Middle East, and that 205 flights were cancelled yesterday (3) alone, of which 107 were arrivals, and 98 were departures from BIA. Speaking after a high-level discussion held yesterday, the Minister said, “A total of 205 flights scheduled to operate to and from Sri Lanka yesterday morning had to be cancelled due to the regional crisis. Of these, 107 were scheduled arrival flights, and 98 were departure flights.” A meeting on the current situation in the aviation sector, in light of the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, was held at the Civil Aviation Ministry premises. The discussion was chaired by the Minister of Ports and Civil Aviation, Anura Karunathilaka, Deputy Minister Janitha Ruwan Kodithuwakku, and Ministry Secretary W.W.S. Mangala. The Personal Secretary to the Minister of Foreign Affairs, the Chairman and Director General of the Civil Aviation Authority, representatives of Airport and Aviation Services (Sri Lanka) Ltd., representatives of SriLankan Airlines, and representatives of all airlines operating in the Gulf region — including Etihad Airways, Gulf Air, Saudia Airlines, Emirates, Qatar Airways, flydubai, Salam Air, Jazeera Airways, Air India, and Air Arabia — participated in the discussion. Although airspace in certain Middle Eastern countries, such as Oman and Saudi Arabia, has been reopened, not all scheduled flights can resume operations. In some areas — including Abu Dhabi, Sharjah, and Dubai — airspace has been opened only for limited timeframes. Operations in these regions are currently restricted to special permit flights, with normal commercial services yet to fully resume, the Minister said. title: Despite Middle East conflict: President assures no fuel shortage
summary: By Sandasen Marasinghe President Anura Kumara Dissanayake assured Parliament yesterday (3) that the country would not face a fuel shortage despite the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. He said that the country had a stock of fuel sufficient for 33 days as of yesterday, and with the arrival of a shipment on 7 March, it would increase to 40 days. He added that another four fuel ships are scheduled to arrive by 28 March. He confirmed that those ships are already loaded, the supply is confirmed, and with the arrival of these stocks, the country would not face any fuel shortage, given the existing conflict situation in the Middle East. He also said that Sri Lanka expects the parties involved in the conflict to choose the path of peace, as there are no victors in war. He further noted that such a conflict would affect the global economy, including Sri Lanka’s. The President added that the country has a stock of diesel sufficient for the next 33 days and petrol for the next 27 days. He stated that a fuel ship carrying 35,000 MT of petrol is expected to arrive in Sri Lanka on 7 or 8 March. A ship containing fuel from RM Parks is expected on 14 March, from SINOPEC on 17 March, from Indian Oil Company (IOC) on 21 March, and from Ceylon Petroleum Corporation on 28 March. He assured that all the ships are loaded and that supply and storage have been confirmed. Regarding aviation fuel, he said that the country requires only 1,800 MT, of which Sri Lanka refines 1,060 MT and the remainder is imported. The available stocks are sufficient for 49 days. He added that stocks of crude oil sufficient for 44 days are available for refining. The President noted that ships are being brought in based on the availability of storage and existing fuel stocks. He added, however, that if the war situation worsens in the coming days, the situation could change, as it would have a global impact. title: Turning the page, continuing the journey
summary: Dear readers, Today marks the publication of the final daily print edition ofCeylon Today. This is not a moment we approach lightly. For little over 14 years, the daily edition has been part of your mornings – folded into briefcases, shared across office desks, read over tea, and debated in homes across the country. To have been welcomed into your daily lives has been both a privilege and a profound responsibility. The media landscape, in Sri Lanka and across the world, has changed in ways few could have fully anticipated. Technology evolves at an unrelenting pace, reader habits continue to shift, and the economics of print journalism grow ever more complex. After careful reflection, we have taken the difficult decision to cease publication of our daily print edition. Let us assure you: this is not a farewell to journalism, nor a retreat from our principles. Our commitment to accuracy, accountability, and ethical reporting remains unwavering. We will continue to serve the public interest with the same editorial independence and rigour that have defined us since our inception. Importantly, our Sunday edition will continue with renewed purpose. We look forward to bringing you a stronger, richer, and more thoughtfulCeylon Todayeach week: one that offers deeper analysis, broader perspectives, and carefully considered reporting on the issues that matter most. Transitions inevitably carry a note of nostalgia, but they also carry opportunity. As we turn this page, we do so with gratitude for your loyalty and with determination to evolve in ways that better serve you in the years ahead. Thank you for reading us, challenging us, and standing with us. We hope you will continue this journey with us every Sunday, and across our digital platforms, as we strive to deliver journalism worthy of your trust.

title: Amid Middle East, Red Sea disruptions: Colombo Free Zone offers safe cargo routing
summary: By Sulochana Ramiah Mohan Amid the ongoing instability in the Middle East and the Red Sea region, Colombo’s Free Zone operations have been positioned as a secure alternative routing solution for global cargo movements. With shipping lines and airlines facing operational disruptions and heightened security risks in affected zones, logistics operators in Colombo are offering contingency routing options to ensure continuity of trade and delivery commitments. The Colombo Free Zone is facilitating multiple routing combinations, including sea-to-sea (SEA/SEA), sea-to-air (SEA to AIR), air-to-sea (AIR to SEA), and air-to-air (AIR/AIR) transfers. The scope of services includes cross-stuffing, palletising, re-documentation, short-term storage, and onward booking — all conducted under Free Zone status, ensuring there is no duty impact on cargo in transit. Industry sources said the alternative routing mechanism enables shippers to bypass high-risk maritime and air corridors while effectively managing transit delays caused by the regional crisis. Logistics stakeholders noted that the initiative aims to provide immediate, flexible solutions for shipments requiring contingency arrangements, positioning Colombo as a reliable transshipment and redistribution hub during the ongoing geopolitical uncertainty.
